title: EPPS 6302
text:
R-package Google trends data vs. Downloaded data on Google trends.

Differences: The gtrendsR package is a lot more in depth than the Google Trends version however, Google Trends is easier to access. Google trends doesn’t have the ability to manipulate data or change how it is viewed but it does allow you to search in specific time frames as well as location and type of search.



Text Analysis

Analyze Biden-Xi Summit data:
The most important terms in this topic are China, Corona virus, Biden, Xijinping, americans, fentanyl. This suggests that the summit was focusing on US-China relations and different aspects of it. There is also a separate cluster related to the Uyghur genocide which was a big topic of interest in the United States with some celebrities and athletes talking about it. Other topics of interst include taiwan and ccp which are just places close to China and has nothing to do with China-US relations.

Analyze U.S. Presidential Inaugural Speeches:
The use of the words “american” and “people” are fairly often in the speeches of many U.S. presidents. There are some presidents that have don’t use them often such as Bush and Kennedy and then you have a fair share that use it heavily such as Reagan and Clinton. The lack of “american” and “people” during Bush’s first speech in 2001 compared to his second one in 2005 could be indicative of the effects of 9/11. There was a massive increase in the use of those words after that event with Obama, Trump, and Biden all using it more than Bush did in 2001. This could also show a shift in politics as there was beginning to be more focus on american policies rather than foreign affairs.
Wordfish:
Wordfish is a Poisson scaling model. It allows you to scale documents without needing to reference scores/texts and it uses unsupervised text scaling methods. It uses observed word frequencies to find positions of documents.



Some difficulties I found while doing the scraping is that one portion of the code failed to work. The code failed to find govfiles1 which stopped the program from working. I would consider the data usable to an extent. The biggest issue was that the columns weren’t ranked. This meant that we couldn’t see which ones were the highest and which values were the lowest. This would be an important thing to improve if I were to run this code again. I would also look to add color to the presentation in order to make it more visually appealing.



When I was running the code provided for the text analysis of YouTube comments for CNN, I was unable to get the data because I reached my query limit. You can definitely use quanteda to analyze this data as well. Quanteda would allow us to see focal words in a much easier way. Key points of comment section data would become highlighted or placed in the center.

Three applications that I use that employ a database system that accesses persistent data:
NBA.com: Website created by the National Basketball Association that has news of basketball games, players, teams. Website also includes statistics for players and teams as well as a platform to watch full games, highlights, and talk shows.

Amazon.com: E-commerce platform that has products, shipping information, entertainment, and pharmacy.
Three applications in domain projects:
NBA Betting Asssistant:

Purpose: Track recent performances of players against each team, highlight different factors that affected match ups such as injuries or suspensions. Allows betters to make better decisions when placing bets.
Functions:

Show recent player stats against speciifc teams (previous 10 games) as well as highlight which players were injured or missing in previous matchups.
Show which players are injured or suspended in current matchup.
Show spread, over/under, and historical data of how team has performed.

Design:

Home page that has upcoming games as well as betting props.
Search bar to lookup specific player and shows recent performance against upcoming team (ex: Kyrie Irving’s stats in the past 10 games against the LA Lakers).
Section that shows historical performance of team against the spread.


Cooking Aid:

Purpose: Help in the kitchen by allowing users to feed ingredients into database and it will show popular recipes that can be made. It will also provide replacements for ingredients and a section for reviews and recommendations.
Functions:

Ingredient input: Users put in any ingredient they have and it will respond with recipes that you can create or recipes that require one more ingredient.
Ingredient Substitution: Provides substitutions for ingredients for people who are allergic or trying to be healthier (ex: yogurt for sour cream).
Forum for reviews, pictures, recommendations
Nutritional Information: Calories, Protein, and other info

Design:

Home page with popular recipes
Search bar to input ingredients and results will show recipes as well as close matches
Pop-up for substitutions of ingredients provided
Comment section that has option to leave comments, recommendations, and pcitures


Grocery Tracker:

Purpose: Assist with tracking groceries and decreasing waste.
Functions:

Grocery input: Identify each grocery as well as expiry date
Will automatically prioritize groceries depending on which one expires the quickest
Creates a grocery list with items that are either finished, expired, or close to expired

Design:

Home page showing a list of groceries in pantry, fridge, and freezer
Foods that are close to expiration are at the top of the list
Separate link for grocery shopping that will show a grocery list with indications for products that are either finished, expired, or close to expiry.


Importance of Data Mining:
Even though data can be retrieved effectively and efficiently, data mining is still necessary because it allows us to find certain trends and patterns within data sets that will help us find solutions to problems.



Three tables used to store information in social networks:

Likes Table: Table that stores information over user likes such as orignal post, time when interacted, original poster, amount of total likes, paid product placement or not.
Call Log Table: Table that stores information of call logs between users. Contents of table could include; type of call (video or voice), length of call, call recipient, amount of calls, and time of call.
Post Table: Table that stores user post and information regarding post. Contents could include: Post, type of post (video, photo, slideshow, gif), time of post, comments, likes, shares, location of post, and views.

title: Assignment 2
text:
Difference between relation schema, relation, and instance:

Relation schema is a diagram or blueprint of the table. It defines the attributes and what is supposed to be inside each tuple without actually having real data.
Relation is a table that follows the rules of the relation schema. It contains real data that the schema defines and has attributes and tuples.
Instance is the table at any particular moment in time. It provides a picture of the data at one speciifc moment. The instance can chance as time moves on but it will still follow the schema.
Example: In a university database, there could be a table for Courses. The relation schema would be a blueprint of the table and it would look something like this:
Courses(CourseID: INT, Course_Name: VARCHAR, Professor: VARCHAR, Credits: INT)
The schema is showing that the Courses table would have attributes for Course ID which would be an integer, Course Name which is a string, Professor which is a string, and Credits which is an integer. The relation would be an actual table with real data for each course. The instance would be the data at one particular time. If the data changes, for instance, a new course was added, then that would be a new instance.

title: Assignment 5
text:
E-R Diagram definitions:
a)

A disconnected graph means that there are entities that are not related to the rest of schema. This could possibly mean that there is incomplete data.

b)

A graph that has a cycle means that there are relationships that are forming loops. This means that there might be redundancy within the data.




Weak entity sets exist because they allow us to avoid redudancy and make it easier to do queries. For example, doing inner and outer joins between multiple tables because of adding something like a unique_id to a table makes the entire process much less efficient.
SQL Exercise:



i)
select e.ID and e.person_name
from employee
join works on e.ID = w.ID
join company on w.company_name = c.company_name
where e.city = c.city
ii)
select e.ID and e.person_name
from employee
join manages on e.ID = m.ID
join employee mgr on m.manager_id = mgr.ID
where e.city = mgr.city and e.street = mgr.street
iii)
with avgsalary as (
     select company_name, avg(salary) as avg_salary

     from works

     group by company_name
)
select e.ID and e.person_name
from employee
join works on e.ID = w.ID
join avgsalary on w.company_name = a.company_name
where w.salary > a.avg_salary



The query uses natural join to connect all the different tables which can result in incorrect results since there are multiple tables that share column names. Data could also be omitted altogether because natural join does not include rows where the join columns do not match. It would be smarter to use explicit join conditions.
